title: El recibo de la luz en la colonia Roma

dialogue.speaker: Mateo
dialogue.spanish: Oye, Lucía, no te pases... Acabo de ver el recibo de la luz de este bimestre y casi me da un infarto.
dialogue.english: Hey, Lucía, come on now... I just saw this two-month electricity bill and I almost had a heart attack.

slang.actualMeaning: come on / don't go too far / you're kidding me
slang.example: ¡No te pases, te comiste todo el pastel!

dialogue.speaker: Lucía
dialogue.spanish: Aguanta, Mateo, pues no te esponjes. Es que la semana pasada hizo un frío horrible y dejé el calentador eléctrico prendido.
dialogue.english: Hold on, Mateo, well don't get worked up. Last week it was freezing cold and I left the electric space heater on.

slang.actualMeaning: don't get puffed up / don't get worked up or angry
slang.example: Tranquilo, no te esponjes, fue solo una broma.

dialogue.speaker: Mateo
dialogue.spanish: ¡Pero si subió al doble! O sea, tú sabes que ahorita ando bien bruja porque no me han pagado el proyecto de diseño.
dialogue.english: It doubled! I mean, you know I'm super broke right now because they haven't paid me for the design project yet.

slang.actualMeaning: I'm completely broke / out of money (Mexican idiom)
slang.example: Fin de quincena y ya ando bien bruja.

dialogue.speaker: Lucía
dialogue.spanish: Bueno, tranquilo, mi primo Javi me debía una lana de los boletos del concierto y me acaba de transferir.
dialogue.english: Well, relax, my cousin Javi owed me cash for the concert tickets and he just sent me a transfer.

dialogue.speaker: Mateo
dialogue.spanish: Uf, qué alivio... Porque el casero ya me estaba mandando mensajes por WhatsApp desde las ocho de la mañana.
dialogue.english: Phew, what a relief... Because the landlord was already sending me messages on WhatsApp since eight in the morning.

dialogue.speaker: Lucía
dialogue.spanish: Yo pongo el setenta por ciento ahorita en la app y te invito unos esquites si me echas la mano con las cajas de la bodega.
dialogue.english: I'll pay seventy percent right now in the app and treat you to some corn cups if you give me a hand with the storage room boxes.

questions.question: What caused the two-month electricity bill in Mateo and Lucía's apartment to double?
options: Lucía left the electric space heater on during freezing nights last week
Mateo left his computer running day and night
The landlord billed them for the whole building
questions.explanation: Lucía admits she left the electric space heater on ('dejé el calentador eléctrico prendido').

questions.question: Why is Mateo broke right now, and how much of the bill does Lucía agree to cover?
options: He hasn't been paid for his design project yet; Lucía covers 70% of the bill
He bought concert tickets; Lucía covers 50% of the bill
He lost his wallet; Lucía covers 100% of the bill
He paid the water bill; Lucía covers 30% of the bill
questions.explanation: Mateo hasn't been paid for his design project yet, and Lucía covers 70% after her cousin Javi paid her back.

questions.question: What favor does Lucía ask of Mateo in exchange for treating him to 'esquites'?
options: Help her with the boxes in the storage room ('la bodega')
Walk her dog in the park
questions.explanation: Lucía says: 'te invito unos esquites si me echas la mano con las cajas de la bodega.'

questions.question: Slang Side Quest: What do 'no te pases', 'no te esponjes', and 'andar bien bruja' mean in Mexican Spanish?
options: 'No te pases' = come on/don't go too far; 'no te esponjes' = don't get worked up; 'andar bruja' = to be broke
'No te pases' = don't walk by; 'no te esponjes' = don't get wet; 'andar bruja' = to stay up late
'No te pases' = hurry up; 'no te esponjes' = don't eat too much; 'andar bruja' = to be angry
'No te pases' = excuse me; 'no te esponjes' = don't fall asleep; 'andar bruja' = to be lucky
questions.explanation: 'No te pases' means 'come on!', 'no te esponjes' means 'don't get puffed up/angry', and 'andar bruja' means to be broke!
